title: Fibre products distribute over a finite coproduct
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of morphisms of schemes, and put $V=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ with its induced morphism to $X$. For every integer $p\ge0$, there is a canonical isomorphism of schemes over $X$ $$V\times_X\cdots\times_XV\;\cong\;\coprod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}} U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p},$$ with $p+1$ factors on the left. Under this isomorphism, every projection omitting a factor restricts on the summand indexed by $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$ to the corresponding projection between the indexed fibre products.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes), applied to the disjoint coproduct pieces, together with the universal property of fibre products in Section 26.17

proof.text: Work in the category of schemes over X, whose finite products are the iterated fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. The scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] is also a coproduct in Over X because the forgetful functor creates and reflects colimits. Form the cofan with vertex the n-fold product of V and component at J the product lift of the maps pi_r followed by iota_(J r).

The forgetful functor Over X to Scheme preserves pullbacks and finite coproducts and reflects isomorphisms. Mathlib finitaryExtensive_of_preserves_and_reflects_isomorphism therefore transfers the extensive structure of Scheme to Over X. Prove that the canonical cofan is a colimit by induction on n, including n=0: there is exactly one empty index tuple, and the empty products identify by their universal properties.

For the successor, reindex tuples by their first coordinate and remaining coordinates using Fin.cons. Split each (n+1)-fold product into a binary product of its first factor and its n-fold tail; the limiting binary fan follows directly from product lifts and extensionality. Both the original coproduct and the tail cofan are universal finite coproducts by FinitaryPreExtensive.isUniversal_finiteCoproducts. Apply IsUniversalColimit.nonempty_isColimit_prod_of_isPullback to these two cofans, interpreting binary products as pullbacks over the terminal object. This applies the base-change distribution [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] in both arguments and flattens the resulting coproduct. Its component equations are Pi.lift_pi and the Fin.cons equations. Reindexing back gives the desired colimit cofan.

For n=p+1, compare this colimit cofan with the chosen coproduct using coconePointUniqueUpToIso. The colimit comparison equations followed by the product projections give exactly the component identities. For each omitted-factor projection, apply Pi.hom_ext; after composing with a remaining coordinate, rewrite both sides by the component identities and Pi.lift_pi. This proves all omitted-factor compatibility equations.

lean.statement: theorem etale_fibre_product_coproduct (X : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type v) [Finite I] (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (u : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X) : let A : I → Over X := fun i => Over.mk (u i) let V : Over X := Over.mk (Sigma.desc u) let P := fun (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 1) → I) => ∏ᶜ fun r => A (J r) let Q := fun p : ℕ => ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin (p + 1) => V let c : ∀ i : I, A i ⟶ V := fun i => Over.homMk (Sigma.ι U i) (Sigma.ι_desc u i) ∃ e : ∀ p : ℕ, (∐ P p) ≅ Q p, (∀ (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 1) → I) (r : Fin (p + 1)), Sigma.ι (P p) J ≫ (e p).hom ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (p + 1) => V) r = Pi.π (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => A (J s)) r ≫ c (J r)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 2) → I) (r : Fin (p + 2)), Sigma.ι (P (p + 1)) J ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom ≫ Pi.lift (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (p + 2) => V) (r.succAbove s)) = Pi.lift (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => Pi.π (fun t : Fin (p + 2) => A (J t)) (r.succAbove s)) ≫ Sigma.ι (P p) (fun s => J (r.succAbove s)) ≫ (e p).hom)
